To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV infects and kills DC, and that DC initiate primary T cell proliferation and cytotoxic responses to HIV but also disseminate HIV to T cells.
dendritic cells are the first cells to be infected with HIV and the first cells to initiate the immune response to HIV.
dendritic cells (DC) initiate primary proliferative responses to HIV in vitro but disseminate virus and that the capacity of DC in HIV infection to stimulate T cells is compromised.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DC in HIV infection and with the development of strategies that may be useful to promote immunity in HIV infected individuals.
the interaction of DC with T cells and HIV.
the function of DC in HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV infection is characterized by a progressive failure to initiate T cell responses and that this failure is due to progressive inhibition of the function of DC to transfer antigen.
HIV infection is a disease of DC and that DC are the key to the development of immunotherapies for HIV infection.
DC are involved in both HIV dissemination and the generation of protective immunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV 1 infection is associated with changes in DC function that promote viral dissemination but inhibit the development of protective T cell immunity.
HIV infection in humans involves a complex interaction of DC, T cells, and virus that leads to a balance between immune activation and viral dissemination.
DC in HIV infection are compromised in their capacity to initiate a primary T cell response to HIV, while retaining the capacity to promote B cell antibody production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DC are the key players in HIV infection and that DC may be used as a therapeutic target to prevent HIV infection and to treat HIV infection.
HIV infection can be seen as a disease of the dendritic cell (DC), and DC are the key cells in HIV transmission and in the development of immunity and disease progression.
DC are not just a conduit for virus dissemination, they are the major antigen presenting cells in HIV infection and they are the major targets for HIV infection.
